thread:
anna: Heads up — got two restore jobs in staging failing with AccessDenied during decrypt. Error: "KMS:Decrypt AccessDenied". Not sure if this is a permissions drift or KMS grant TTL expiry. Anyone seen similar this morning?

mike: Which key id? any recent RBAC churn?

anna: Key is arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333444:key/abc-123-xyz. No manual IAM edits logged in the last 6h, but we had a service-account role rename merged yesterday (ENG-1182).

sec-bot: [alert] 2024-10-07T08:02:14Z - kms-grant-expiry - grantId=G-98765 keyId=abc-123-xyz principal=roles/kms-uploader ttl=2024-10-07T07:59:00Z

jamie: That alert matches. The uploader role rotation script (PR #422) changed the serviceAccount name but we forgot to recreate the ephemeral grant mapping. Likely grants expired and auto-renewal didn't find the new principal.

mike: Can you paste the relevant audit log line? also do a quick `aws kms list-grants --key-id abc-123-xyz` in staging.

anna: Paste from audit: `eventTime=2024-10-07T07:59:03Z userIdentity=ci/uploader role=roles/kms-uploader action=CreateGrant result=Denied reason=PrincipalNotFound`.

anna: Running list-grants now...

anna: ```
> aws kms list-grants --key-id abc-123-xyz
Grants:
- GrantId: G-98765
  GranteePrincipal: arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/old-uploader-role
  CreationDate: 2024-04-07T07:59:00Z
  RetiringPrincipal: arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/enc-ops
```

jamie: There it is — grant points to the old role name. When the role was renamed the grant couldn't be renewed and then TTL expired. Two important takeaways: (1) our grant-renewal automation doesn't validate principal existence before renewing; (2) we lack a fast detection alert for grant -> principal mismatch.

mike: Agreed. Immediate mitigation: create a short-lived grant that maps the new role -> run restore test. We should also add a preflight check into the role-rename playbook. I'll create a short grant now if anna ok with me using the CMK.

anna: go for it. tag me when done. :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: I can run the restore-sim after the grant is created. ETA 15m.

mike: Created grant G-99801 mapping arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/new-uploader-role -> key/abc-123-xyz, GrantTokens=[gtn-1], expiry=2024-10-07T09:00:00Z.

ops-oncall: Running restore-sim: `./scripts/restore-sim --env=staging --snapshot=snap-20241006`

ops-oncall: Restore-sim log snippet: `2024-10-07T08:14:02Z INFO decrypting snapshot parts... success` — looks good. :tada:

jamie: For follow-up: I propose a 3-part fix: 1) Add preflight principal existence check to role rename playbook; 2) Enhance grant-renewer to rebind grants when principal canonical alias detected; 3) Add alert rule: if grant principal != current IAM ARN for service-account for >5m raise P1.

mike: +1. I'll open a ticket with remediation steps and include sample commands for ops:
```
# validate grant principal
aws kms list-grants --key-id abc-123-xyz | jq '.Grants[] | select(.GrantId=="G-98765")'
# create new grant
aws kms create-grant --key-id abc-123-xyz --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/new-uploader-role --operations Decrypt Encrypt --name "temp-restore-grant"
```

anna: Also: let's add a linchpin test to our staging RBAC suite to rename the role and verify grant renewal path. Cc @sec-bot for automated ticketing of any future grant expirations.

sec-bot: Noted. Will create automated incident when grant principal mismatch persists for >5m.

ops-oncall: Filing postmortem stub now and linking PRs. I'll schedule a 30m follow-up to run through the playbook updates.

anna: Thanks everyone. Closing the immediate incident — moving this to encops backlog (ENG-4287).
